baseline.scope: Reconciled source review and parent-provided credential-free scan artifacts; not a production penetration test or runtime attestation.

notes: Tool advisory paths are alternative dependency graph paths and are never summed into vulnerability totals.
The four dependency advisory families are kept distinct from custom source findings and from owner/deployment verification gates.
Status describes the strength and scope of evidence, not whether a deployment is secure or a remediation is activated.
Custom source-confirmed findings include an architectural revocation limitation; this is not a count of reproduced external exploits.

deduplication.method: One stable identifier per materially distinct attack path, custody risk, or verification gate. Cross-domain overlapping controls are linked through prior IDs rather than duplicated.
not_duplicated: AUTH-003 is specific to email-auth admission; HTTP-001 is the broader distributed transport/edge gate.
ACCESS-002 is bootstrap-principal exposure; ACCESS-003 is trusted-server RLS scope; ACCESS-004 is deployment-state evidence.
MEDIA-002 is object deletion/retention; OPS-005 is recovery-evidence availability and integrity.
DEP-001 through DEP-004 are one record per advisory family, not one record per package path.

findings.domain: Authentication, identity and session security
findings.title: A valid but not freshly reauthenticated session can add a durable attacker-controlled email credential
evidence: server/_core/email-auth.ts:891-931 accepts authenticateRequest as the account proof, links a verified email identity, and issues a session without a recent-primary-authentication assertion.
server/_core/email-identity.ts:329-375 persists the unique subject-to-user mapping after current-actor checks.
shared/const.ts:4-5 permits a 12-hour application session; server/_core/sdk.ts:520-589 accepts valid durable actor-bound sessions without a recent-auth claim.
tests/email-auth-server.test.ts:406-450 and tests/email-identity.test.ts:110-134 cover current actor authority/mapping uniqueness, not enrollment freshness.
findings.preconditions: Optional email authentication is enabled; an attacker has a victim's active Circles web session or native bearer and controls a confirmed provider email/password identity. Deployment enablement was not inspected.
findings.impact: The attacker can attach their email identity, receive a new session, and retain a later authentication route after the stolen session expires or is revoked. This turns temporary session compromise into persistent account access.
findings.remediation: Require a server-verified, short-lived, single-use recent-primary-authentication intent bound to the numeric actor before credential enrollment. Define inventory, removal, recovery, notification, and session-lifecycle behavior.
findings.acceptance: Isolated stale/replayed/mismatched-proof negative tests and authorized synthetic-account staging prove enrollment, session revocation, removal/recovery, and notifications. No live validation was performed.
findings.reachability: API and native/web account credential enrollment path.
findings.approval_boundary: Provider settings, notification delivery, and account testing require separate authorization.

findings.domain: Authentication, identity and session security
findings.title: Configuration permits a remote HTTP frontend origin in credentialed OAuth and email flows
evidence: server/_core/frontend-origins.ts:17-38 accepts canonical http: and https: origins without a production-only HTTPS rule.
server/_core/cors.ts:21-35,73-123 and server/_core/email-auth.ts:219-255 use that trust set for credentialed CORS and browser email admission.
server/_core/oauth.ts:207-230 permits a configured http: web callback; server/_core/cookies.ts:35-44 supports secure cross-origin cookie contexts.
findings.preconditions: A production-like deployment configures a non-loopback HTTP frontend origin and a user has an API cookie; an on-path attacker or party controlling that origin can modify its script.
findings.impact: The insecure frontend becomes trusted for OAuth redirects, email browser admission, and credentialed CORS, allowing manipulated frontend code to originate authenticated API requests.
findings.remediation: Reject non-loopback HTTP frontend origins in production validation; retain HTTP only for explicit direct-loopback development and attest deployed OAuth/CORS/frontend origins.
findings.acceptance: Production-mode tests reject remote HTTP origins; authorized staging browser tests verify configured origins, CORS, redirects, and cookie behavior.
findings.reachability: Deployment configuration affecting API and web OAuth/email flows.
findings.approval_boundary: Deployment configuration attestation is separate from source work.

findings.domain: Authentication, identity and session security
findings.title: Email password admission limits are explicitly process-local
evidence: server/_core/email-auth.ts:644-755 implements in-memory account, network, and global budgets and documents their process-local defense-in-depth role at :664-669.
server/_core/email-auth.ts:823-839,860-878,891-907 apply the local budgets to sign-in, sign-up, and connect.
tests/sec27-auth-security.test.ts:251-317 proves independent bounded in-process budgets, not shared enforcement.
findings.preconditions: Email authentication runs on multiple replicas without sufficiently strict shared provider/edge controls, and an attacker distributes attempts across replicas or sources.
findings.impact: Effective sign-in, sign-up, and connect budgets can multiply by replica count, weakening password-guessing and abuse resistance.
findings.remediation: Require reviewed shared account-aware provider/edge throttling and privacy-preserving account/source/global admission policy before scaling email authentication.
findings.acceptance: Authorized non-production multi-replica/edge test demonstrates shared distributed admission and provider-unavailable behavior.
findings.reachability: Email authentication API; conditional on deployment topology and edge controls.
findings.approval_boundary: Provider and edge controls require separate operational review.

findings.domain: Authentication, identity and session security
findings.title: Provider-side email confirmation, recovery, and lifecycle controls lack deployment evidence
evidence: server/_core/email-auth.ts:150-165 pins expected provider origin/key format; :525-573 validates provider subject, confirmed email, and email identity.
server/_core/email-auth.ts:575-608,860-885 implements confirmation-only signup without exposing provider credentials or minting a session.
No scoped application-owned reset/recovery route or screen establishes provider confirmation, redirect allowlists, disable/delete, or recovery policy.
findings.preconditions: Email authentication is enabled in a deployment; assurance depends on provider project configuration and operational recovery/deletion policy.
findings.impact: A provider misconfiguration could weaken confirmation/recovery assurance or leave post-compromise recovery incomplete; no misconfiguration was observed.
findings.remediation: Document and attest provider confirmation, password, recovery redirect, rate-limit, token/session, disable/delete, support, and recovery controls aligned with AUTH-001.
findings.acceptance: With owner approval and synthetic non-production accounts only, inspect settings and exercise confirmation/recovery lifecycle.
findings.reachability: Provider-managed identity lifecycle.
findings.approval_boundary: No provider request was made in this audit.

findings.domain: Authorization, database isolation and private-resource access
findings.title: Direct-message creation can force public materialization of an unprofiled target's private identity
evidence: server/social-router.ts:762-764 exposes protected social.openDirect with caller-selected targetUserId; server/social-service.ts:3161-3170 checks only target existence before ensureProfileWithDb for both parties.
server/social-service.ts:548-579 reads users.name and inserts a persistent profile when absent; :628-634 describes ordinary self materialization.
server/social-router.ts:518-544 and server/social-service.ts:863-894 expose public profile list/page/detail reads without a per-account visibility predicate.
server/moderation-service.ts:284-293 identifies users.name as OAuth/private identity; tests/database-remediation-db15.test.ts:107-115 lacks absent-target materialization/public-exposure coverage.
findings.preconditions: An authenticated Circles account knows a valid numeric target user ID and the target has no social profile.
findings.impact: A caller can create an unsolicited direct conversation and persist a publicly discoverable profile with the target's OAuth-derived name and predictable handle. The endpoint outcome also probes account existence. It does not expose email, OpenID, sessions, or other users fields through this path.
findings.remediation: Define direct-message identity/consent rules; do not persist a recipient public profile as a caller side effect. Use conversation-scoped display data or require opt-in/existing public profile and decide whether relationship/DM consent is required.
findings.acceptance: Service/router regressions verify guest profile/page reads do not reveal an absent target's private source name after DM-open unless chosen policy permits it; cover nonexistent target, existing profile, retry, and concurrent opens.
findings.reachability: Authenticated social direct-message opening followed by public/guest profile reads.
findings.approval_boundary: No live database verification was performed.

findings.domain: Authorization, database isolation and private-resource access
findings.title: Active database pool retains a privileged bootstrap principal
evidence: server/_core/postgres-config.mjs:9-15 defines postgres as CURRENT_CONNECTION_PRINCIPAL while a dedicated bootstrap identity is proposed only.
drizzle/postgres/0000_circles_app.sql:5-10 grants the runtime role to postgres.
server/runtime-role-pool.ts:560-628 guards role/session-reset SQL and sets/verifies restricted role; server/db.ts:30-65 creates only the guarded pool.
findings.preconditions: Application-code execution/raw SQL bypasses the pool guard, privileged connection credentials are accessed directly, or configuration permits use before SET ROLE.
findings.impact: The more-authoritative bootstrap principal can bypass the intended runtime-role database boundary and access private resources.
findings.remediation: Complete owner-approved dedicated LOGIN bootstrap cutover with SET-only membership, reviewed DSN/connection update, and exact session/effective-role startup attestation.
findings.acceptance: Owner-controlled disposable environment proves dedicated session principal, restricted effective role, SET-only membership, and socket destruction on initialization/cleanup failure.
findings.reachability: Server/database credential or internal execution boundary; not direct browser database access.
findings.approval_boundary: Role provisioning, DSN changes, and startup validation require owner authorization.

findings.domain: Authorization, database isolation and private-resource access
findings.title: Runtime-role RLS is a trusted-server boundary rather than user/circle row isolation
evidence: drizzle/postgres/0000_circles_app.sql:289-333 enables RLS but grants circles_app_runtime universal USING (true) WITH CHECK (true) policies.
operations/migrations/0010_circles_activity_inbox.sql:60-88 and 0012_circles_moderation.sql:70-95 use the same runtime-policy model.
operations/migrations/0023_circles_ops_policy_health.sql:36-74 accepts those true-predicate runtime policies as reviewed state.
findings.preconditions: A server authorization flaw, unsafe new runtime-role query/endpoint, arbitrary SQL under runtime role, or incorrect internal consumer crosses the trusted server boundary.
findings.impact: Policies do not constrain recipient, actor, membership, or moderator scope after server boundary failure; affected records can include direct messages, social content, Activity, and moderation data. Ordinary external callers cannot directly query these tables under reviewed browser-role denial.
findings.remediation: Design phased table-specific actor-bound RLS while retaining service authorization. Set trusted actor context transaction-locally only, never from tRPC input, headers, or cookies; begin with Activity and direct/circle conversations.
findings.acceptance: Disposable PostgreSQL integration proves cross-recipient Activity, nonparticipant DM, revoked-private-member, and unauthorized moderation denial plus legitimate runtime/admin maintenance paths; exact policies/ACLs/force-RLS/functions are attested before rollout.
findings.reachability: Defense in depth after internal/server compromise or logic failure.
findings.approval_boundary: RLS rollout needs explicit database-owner review for admin/background/revocation compatibility.

findings.domain: Authorization, database isolation and private-resource access
findings.title: Static review cannot establish deployed database catalog or prepared-migration activation state
evidence: operations/migrations/0017_circles_dedicated_app_login.sql:1-9, 0015_circles_publish_post_receipts.sql:1-4, and 0025_circles_media_upload_budget.sql:1-6 explicitly describe prepared-only state.
operations/tests/current-authorization-contract.node.mjs validates checked-in fixtures/evaluator rather than a live PostgreSQL catalog.
findings.preconditions: Any claim about deployed ACL, RLS, trigger, role, function, or migration state requires live catalog evidence.
findings.impact: This is not an exploitable condition; it prevents confirmation that deployment matches reviewed source and static contracts.
findings.remediation: Maintain a value-free owner-run release attestation for migration journal, ownership, ACLs, policies, RLS/force-RLS, triggers/functions/search paths, role attributes/membership, and session/effective role.
findings.acceptance: Authorized controlled read-only catalog/readiness checks produce redacted aggregate pass/fail evidence and reconcile exact migration-journal entries.
findings.reachability: Deployment state.
findings.approval_boundary: Live database reads were prohibited for this audit.

findings.domain: Media encryption, upload validation, and storage transport
findings.title: Signing-secret compromise or rotation has media-wide impact through key coupling
evidence: server/social-service.ts:180-203 derives the AES-256-GCM media key from the managed signing secret plus circles-media-v1; :206-236 repeats derivation for decryption.
server/_core/env.ts:71-80 defines application signing/cookie-secret configuration; README.md:29,48 documents current coupling.
findings.preconditions: An attacker obtains the managed signing secret and ciphertext objects, or an operator rotates the secret without compatible media-key migration.
findings.impact: Signing-secret compromise can extend to decryption of acquired historical media; uncoordinated rotation can make historical media unreadable. Ciphertext access remains required for confidentiality impact.
findings.remediation: Use a separately managed versioned media root key with key identifiers, dual-read migration, rotation/recovery procedures, and isolated rotation tests. Do not use signing-secret rotation as logout mitigation.
findings.acceptance: Key-version round-trip, old/new dual-read, tamper, unsupported-version, and rotation/recovery tests pass before any approved custody rollout.
findings.reachability: Encrypted media confidentiality and availability; conditional on secret/ciphertext access or rotation.
findings.approval_boundary: Key provisioning, rotation, and provider recovery require separate authorization.

findings.domain: Media encryption, upload validation, and storage transport
findings.title: Orphaned encrypted provider objects have no source-level deletion or compensation path
evidence: server/social-service.ts:2037-2115 documents/implements discard metadata removal without provider deletion.

server/media-upload-budget.ts:66-69,205-301 preserves failed/ambiguous PUT charges and inventories reconciliation candidates; drizzle/media-upload-budget-schema.ts:52-55 retains reservation rows because no delete API exists.
server/media-upload-budget.ts:12-15 caps an account at 64 objects/512 MiB; server/social-router.ts:809-895 fails closed when ledger unavailable.
findings.preconditions: A permitted account causes failed/ambiguous publication or discard, provider deletion lifecycle is unavailable, and provider retention/cost applies; multi-account behavior can increase aggregate cost.
findings.impact: Opaque encrypted objects and durable quota charges can persist without physical reclamation. This is bounded per account in source and is retention/cost/abuse exposure, not direct plaintext disclosure.
findings.remediation: Obtain provider deletion/retention guarantees and design authorized idempotent deletion, outbox, reconciliation, durable receipts, and attached-media deletion policy.
findings.acceptance: Approved provider integration proves idempotent deletion/retry/reconciliation and retained-charge policy without exposing object or key values.
findings.reachability: Provider media lifecycle after failed/ambiguous upload or discard.
findings.approval_boundary: No provider deletion or retention behavior was tested.

findings.domain: Media encryption, upload validation, and storage transport
findings.title: Account-change image-cache cleanup is asynchronous and failure is ignored outside the logout fence
evidence: hooks/circles-context.tsx:214-219 invokes clearPrivateImageCaches fire-and-forget and swallows rejection before replacement actor admission.
lib/media-cache.ts:26-41 rejects when either cache clear fails; lib/client-session.ts:262-359 and hooks/circles-context.tsx:229-291 retain the stronger logout barrier.
components/media-image.tsx:37-77 scopes bearer to current account/request key but cannot establish SDK decoded-image cache behavior.
findings.preconditions: A shared device changes account outside full logout, cache clear is delayed/rejects, and the native image implementation can render a cached protected resource across accounts.
findings.impact: Old private pixels could temporarily be visible after account replacement. Stale bearer reuse is prevented by source.
findings.remediation: Treat actor replacement as a privacy boundary: await successful protected-cache eviction before admitting the new authenticated subtree, or isolate renderer-cache namespaces per account while retaining logout fence.
findings.acceptance: Regression tests cover replacement failure/delay; physical iOS/Android tests prove no cross-account protected rendering under injected cache-clear failures.
findings.reachability: Native shared-device account switch.
findings.approval_boundary: No physical native cache or rendering test was run.

findings.domain: Media encryption, upload validation, and storage transport
findings.title: Storage-provider, DNS/TLS, ledger, and native media behavior retain source-only proof
evidence: server/storage.ts:66-460 enforces HTTPS origins, public DNS answers, pinned lookup/SNI/TLS, redirect refusal, deadlines, and cancellation.
server/_core/storageProxy.ts:375-801 has reference-aware authorization and final locked recheck before byte enqueue; shared/recorded-video.ts and server/sec27-video-validation.ts bound parsing.
findings.preconditions: Deployment/provider/native runtime differs materially from source assumptions.
findings.impact: This is missing operational proof, not a demonstrated source defect; real provider/network/native behavior could differ.
findings.remediation: Run approved non-destructive staging checks for object ACL/ciphertext posture, configured origin/DNS/TLS/redirect behavior, ledger readiness, revocation timing, no-store behavior, and physical iOS/Android cache/decoder behavior.
findings.acceptance: Redacted staging evidence demonstrates each selected contract or records named blocker with capability disabled.
findings.reachability: Storage provider, network, ledger, and device runtime.
findings.approval_boundary: No provider, real DNS/TLS/CDN, native cache, or hardware decoder was exercised.

findings.domain: HTTP request security and abuse resistance
findings.title: Distributed abuse protection is not configured or evidenced in this repository
evidence: server/_core/index.ts:41-49,83-170 defines bounded process-local transport admission.
server/_core/email-auth.ts:664-755 and server/_core/storageProxy.ts:67-170 define finite in-process email/media controls.
docs/media-download-limits.md:21-24 states edge enforcement is required but not configured; no ingress/CDN/WAF artifact was reviewed.
findings.preconditions: Public API is reachable through multiple replicas/restarts and real CDN/WAF/load balancer lacks equivalent global request, concurrency, body, timeout, and client-identity controls.
findings.impact: Distributed traffic can exceed aggregate assurance of per-worker controls, raising availability/resource-cost exposure; source-local limits still constrain a worker.
findings.remediation: Define provider-neutral global/per-client edge admission for general, media, and email routes with overload response and authoritative client identity rules.
findings.acceptance: Authorized multi-replica test proves quotas survive worker selection/restart and header/address rotation while preserving 429/Retry-After behavior.
findings.reachability: Public API deployment topology.
findings.approval_boundary: This audit did not configure or test edge/CDN/WAF infrastructure.

findings.domain: HTTP request security and abuse resistance
findings.title: Forwarded-client identity protections depend on unverified ingress header sanitization
evidence: server/_core/runtimeSecurity.ts:165-237,366-385 keeps proxy trust opt-in/narrow and requires trusted socket, exact protocol, and one forwarded address.
server/_core/index.ts:419-427 trusts only immediate-hop CIDRs; :235-239 and server/_core/storageProxy.ts:291-299 use req.ip client identities.
.env.example:32-35 requires ingress to strip/recreate forwarding headers, but deployed behavior is not in the repository.
findings.preconditions: Trusted proxy CIDRs are wrong/overbroad, direct listener access exists, or ingress forwards caller-controlled X-Forwarded headers rather than recreating them.
findings.impact: An attacker meeting those infrastructure conditions could steer req.ip admission buckets or forwarded transport context.
findings.remediation: Review listener isolation, exact immediate proxy CIDRs, forwarding-header replacement, and one client-address representation.
findings.acceptance: Non-production real-ingress tests cover direct-listener denial, forged/multiple X-Forwarded-For, forged X-Forwarded-Proto, hop mismatch, and correct rate-bucket identity.
findings.reachability: Ingress/proxy deployment configuration.
findings.approval_boundary: No real ingress was tested.

findings.domain: HTTP request security and abuse resistance
findings.title: Non-production uncaught Express errors can disclose stack detail
evidence: server/_core/index.ts:320-344,465-494 normalizes known errors but forwards unknown errors without a final error middleware after routes.

Installed express@4.22.3 uses finalhandler without a terminal handler at node_modules/express/lib/application.js:159-171; finalhandler uses err.stack outside production at node_modules/finalhandler/index.js:77-82,171-184.
Dockerfile:25-29 sets NODE_ENV=production; package.json dev:server uses NODE_ENV=development.
findings.preconditions: A non-production/debug-configured process is publicly reachable and an error reaches Express finalhandler rather than route/tRPC handling.
findings.impact: A response can disclose stack path and implementation detail; no reachable user-controlled response or production exposure was demonstrated.
findings.remediation: Install terminal API error envelope with generic no-store response and server-only diagnostics, including explicit Express 4 async direct-route rejection design.
findings.acceptance: Injected non-parser middleware/route failures in development and production expose no stack, path, request bytes, or credential data.
findings.reachability: Publicly exposed debug/non-production process only.
findings.approval_boundary: No app listener was started.

findings.domain: Live video signaling, membership and native lifecycle
findings.title: Private membership revocation is not server-enforceable after direct media negotiation
evidence: server/live-router.ts:746-795 produces membership-filtered peer-authority snapshot and :1550-1588 gives it to host only.
components/live-media.web.tsx:465-498,542-575 create/close direct RTCPeerConnections locally; components/live-media.native.tsx:663-698,744-774 mirrors it.
tests/cba01-live-peer-authority.test.ts:25-110 and tests/live-access-terminal.test.ts:39-95 prove conforming clients, not media termination against a modified/disconnected host.
findings.preconditions: A private-stream viewer was admitted and negotiated a peer, then is removed while a compromised or nonconforming host ignores revocation or loses control-plane connectivity while peer transport remains alive.
findings.impact: The server cannot terminate that established direct peer itself. This is an architectural limit of documented P2P delivery, not an unauthenticated join bypass; malicious senders can also independently redistribute content under any architecture.
findings.remediation: Decide whether server termination of app-managed transport is required. If so, plan mediated SFU/media-proxy delivery with revocable authorization; otherwise explicitly accept and disclose the direct-P2P limit. Do not promise prevention of malicious sender redistribution.
findings.acceptance: Approved real WebRTC test measures post-negotiation removal under an adversarial/disconnected host and proves selected policy behavior.
findings.reachability: Private live streams after a user is admitted.
findings.approval_boundary: No real WebRTC session was used; persistence duration is unmeasured.

findings.domain: Live video signaling, membership and native lifecycle
findings.title: Abandoned streams retain signaling payloads without automatic expiry cleanup
evidence: server/live-router.ts:54-66 caps a stream at 512 signals of 32,768 bytes (16 MiB before row overhead).
server/live-router.ts:499-547 ends expired-host stream without deleting liveSignals, while :549-601 explicit end deletes them.
server/live-router.ts:874-893 deletes on later stream operations only; drizzle/live-schema.ts:70-83 and drizzle/postgres/0000_circles_app.sql:219-229 lack matching liveSignals query index.
tests/live-signal-bounds.test.ts:27-128 covers per-stream caps but not expired-lease purge.
findings.preconditions: A live-enabled authenticated host and controlled participants fill bounded valid signal rows and abandon without ending; this repeats across streams.
findings.impact: Expired undiscoverable streams retain signaling rows absent later targeted calls, enabling database-growth abuse and progressively expensive unindexed signal polling.
findings.remediation: Implement automatic abandoned-session cleanup, aggregate retention/storage budget, and poll/deletion indexes matched to predicates.
findings.acceptance: Disposable PostgreSQL tests prove expired-lease cleanup, bounded retention, query plans, and race-safe/idempotent behavior before promotion.
findings.reachability: Authenticated live signaling creation and persistence.
findings.approval_boundary: No live database size, plans, or out-of-band cleanup were inspected.

findings.domain: Live video signaling, membership and native lifecycle
findings.title: TURN credentials are actor-bound but not session-, stream-, or revocation-bound
evidence: server/turn-config.ts:5-10,197-235 issues ten-minute REST credentials named only with expiry and user ID.
server/live-router.ts:225-240,1383-1390,1466-1473 returns credentials on authorized join; leave/end has no application-to-coturn revocation action.
operations/coturn/circles-turnserver.conf.template:25-67 has quotas/private-destination denies; tests/turn-config.test.ts:60-81 validates intended user-bound TTL.
findings.preconditions: A user obtains a valid relay credential and deployed coturn accepts it after leave, removal, or stream end.
findings.impact: Relay entitlement can remain for TTL, enabling bounded quota/bandwidth abuse or post-removal allocation if deployment permits it. This is not a confirmed open relay or SSRF finding.
findings.remediation: Make explicit entitlement/revocation decision; if immediate revocation is required, design provider-compatible session-scoped mechanism and validate quotas, expiry, destination denies, and post-removal behavior.
findings.acceptance: Approved synthetic-coturn test proves selected expiry/revocation and quota posture.
findings.reachability: TURN relay after previously authorized live join.
findings.approval_boundary: Actual coturn allocation semantics and configuration parity were not tested.

findings.domain: Live video signaling, membership and native lifecycle
findings.title: Configured TURN does not force relay-only ICE privacy
evidence: components/live-media.web.tsx:83-99,477-505 and components/live-media.native.tsx:166-215,675-705 pass ICE servers without iceTransportPolicy.
server/live-router.ts:57-58 explicitly declares direct P2P model.
W3C WebRTC Recommendation states relay policy uses only TURN relay candidates: https://www.w3.org/TR/webrtc/.
tests/turn-config.test.ts:89-140 and tests/live-ice-protocol.test.ts:23-91 do not collect real candidates or assert relay-only policy.
findings.preconditions: A permitted participant joins a live session, browser/native exposes non-relay candidates under default policy, and product policy requires participant IP privacy.
findings.impact: TURN availability alone does not prevent remote participant learning/selecting direct candidates where exposed by runtime/NAT topology.
findings.remediation: Set explicit direct-P2P/address-privacy policy. If privacy required, carry relay-only setting through adapters and validate candidate gathering on approved browser/native matrix; otherwise document exposure.
findings.acceptance: Real candidate gathering proves selected policy on supported browser/native/NAT matrix.
findings.reachability: Live participants; conditional on runtime and product privacy policy.
findings.approval_boundary: No browser/native candidate collection was run.

findings.domain: Live video signaling, membership and native lifecycle
findings.title: Deployed chat admission indexes cannot be established from source evidence
evidence: server/live-router.ts:950-1001,1936-2004 performs lock-held chat admission counts before insert.

operations/migrations/0024_circles_live_chat_bounds.sql:1-7 says index migration is prepared only; drizzle/live-schema.ts:97-108 declares matching indexes while drizzle/postgres/0000_circles_app.sql:241-259 lacks them.
tests/cba04-live-chat-bounds.test.ts:85-123 checks source/migration text, not installed plan.
findings.preconditions: Target database lacks prepared 0024 indexes and retained live-chat history becomes large.
findings.impact: Polling and admission counts may sequentially scan while live stream lock is held; production condition is not established.
findings.remediation: Retain owner evidence for migration and a disposable PostgreSQL EXPLAIN/concurrency result for exact poll/count predicates before scaling.
findings.acceptance: Read-only catalog state and disposable query-plan/concurrency evidence show selected indexes and bounded lock behavior.
findings.reachability: Live chat database workload.
findings.approval_boundary: No database read/write was authorized.

findings.domain: CI, secrets, deployment and recovery operations
findings.title: Git staging does not exclude private recovery/key artifacts
evidence: .dockerignore:15-23 excludes recovery/private, encrypted/key, dump, and archive classes from Docker context, but .gitignore:20,36-41,72 does not equivalently cover them.
Offline git check-ignore found representative recovery/private key/archive filename classes are not ignored; no files were created or staged.
findings.preconditions: An operator stores recovery identity, encrypted recovery material, dump, or evidence under checkout and uses broad Git staging.
findings.impact: Sensitive recovery artifact could be committed and retained in repository history. Docker-context exclusion does not protect Git staging.
findings.remediation: Mirror recovery/key exclusions in .gitignore and add tracked-file denylist/CI test; retain requirement that live identities/evidence stay outside checkout.
findings.acceptance: Synthetic filename-only ignore and tracked-file tests, plus credential-free staging rehearsal, demonstrate blocked handling.
findings.reachability: Developer/operator source-control workflow.
findings.approval_boundary: No actual credential material should be created for testing.

findings.domain: CI, secrets, deployment and recovery operations
findings.title: Supervisor forwards server runtime environment to Metro by default
evidence: scripts/lib/dev-supervisor-core.mjs:530-568 builds Metro without cleanEnvironment, clones process.env, and removes only CI, DATABASE_URL, and DRIZZLE_DATABASE_URL.

scripts/lib/dev-supervisor-core.mjs:1043-1048 passes that environment to child; operations/supervision/circles-preview.service.example:19 uses EnvironmentFile and docs/service-supervision.md:66 says other values are preserved.
findings.preconditions: Optional template is installed with server-only values and a Metro/Expo plugin, diagnostic path, dependency compromise, or local process compromise reads Metro environment.
findings.impact: Server-only settings can be copied to a narrower-purpose child, increasing custody/exfiltration surface; no browser bundle disclosure or deployed exploit was shown.
findings.remediation: Use documented minimal Metro environment allowlist and test representative server-only values are absent while intended public Expo values remain.
findings.acceptance: Synthetic supervisor spawn-environment test proves allowlist; host template is separately validated without starting production services.
findings.reachability: Optional local/host preview supervisor deployment.
findings.approval_boundary: No installed unit or live environment was examined.

findings.domain: CI, secrets, deployment and recovery operations
findings.title: Privileged and recovery helpers resolve executables through inherited PATH
evidence: operations/coturn/install-coturn.sh:1 uses /usr/bin/env bash and invokes privileged host tools by bare name, including apt-get at :211-212; mutation needs root plus explicit flags.
scripts/recovery-continuity.mjs:660-666 preserves PATH and :695-733 launches helpers shell:false; :763-770 invokes git by bare name.
findings.preconditions: Privileged coturn or recovery operator invokes the tool with attacker-influenced/unexpectedly writable PATH; coturn also requires root and explicit acknowledgment.
findings.impact: A substituted executable could run with invoking authority, including root or access to transient recovery material.
findings.remediation: Use absolute interpreter, fixed trusted PATH before command expansion, and resolved/allowlisted absolute helper paths for privileged/recovery entrypoints.
findings.acceptance: Synthetic hostile-PATH tests demonstrate trusted helper selection or fail-closed behavior without real install/restore.
findings.reachability: Privileged coturn and recovery operator tooling.
findings.approval_boundary: No real coturn installation or restore was run.

findings.domain: CI, secrets, deployment and recovery operations
findings.title: Locked installs lack a package publication-age guard
evidence: .npmrc:1 has node-linker configuration only and no publication-age policy.
.github/workflows/ci.yml:60-61,228-229 and Dockerfile:10-23 use frozen lockfile installs; Dockerfile:2,25 pins Node base digest and Dockerfile:8 requests fixed pnpm version.
Semgrep reported package_managers.npm.npm-missing-minimum-release-age at .npmrc:1; this is retained as a policy finding, not an active package compromise.
findings.preconditions: A reviewed dependency/lockfile update accepts a compromised/malicious newly published package before ecosystem detection or revocation. Unchanged frozen-lock builds are unaffected.
findings.impact: Supply-chain compromise could execute at installation/build; no malicious package or registry compromise was found.
findings.remediation: At a supported package-manager version, add tested minimum-release-age and exception process while retaining frozen-lock/provenance review.
findings.acceptance: Configuration tests demonstrate a synthetic too-new-package exception and unchanged frozen installs.
findings.reachability: Dependency update and build workflow.
findings.approval_boundary: Package-manager compatibility and lockfile changes need separate review.

findings.domain: CI, secrets, deployment and recovery operations
findings.title: Live encrypted backup and isolated restore evidence remains intentionally unverified
evidence: Offline recovery checker emitted SOURCE_CONTRACT_PASS and SOURCE_PASS_EXTERNAL_RECOVERY_UNVERIFIED.
docs/codebase-audit-remediation-20261029.md:14,30-32,40-43 describes private encrypted-backup activation and provider/key evidence as separately gated.
findings.preconditions: A real incident, restore request, or rollback requires encrypted checkpoint and isolated recovery.
findings.impact: Recovery availability/integrity cannot be asserted from source-only evidence; this does not establish recovery failure or absence of backup.
findings.remediation: Run separately authorized current isolated restore drill with controlled encrypted checkpoint and independently reviewed redacted evidence for integrity, reconciliation, key separation, and cleanup.
findings.acceptance: Record isolation target, checksums, catalog/media-ledger reconciliation, cleanup, and exceptions in value-free evidence.
findings.reachability: Incident recovery.
findings.approval_boundary: Do not connect audit work to providers, production databases, backups, or keys without explicit authorization.

findings.domain: Locked dependency advisories and compatibility exposure
findings.title: Expo Router's locked query decoder can process attacker-controlled deep-link query strings
evidence: raw/pnpm-audit-production.json:57-156 and raw/pnpm-audit-full.json:57-156 report the installed resolution and advisory; full/prod advisory set is identical.
pnpm-lock.yaml:3098-3100,11695-11700 resolves expo-router@57.0.22 > query-string@7.1.3 > decode-uri-component@0.2.2.
node_modules/expo-router/build/react-navigation/core/getStateFromPath.js:40-49,488-500 imports/calls queryString.parse; node_modules/query-string/index.js:1-5 imports decoder.
app.config.ts:24-27,70,89-101 registers custom scheme/browsable Android VIEW filter; app/oauth/callback.tsx:93-101 consumes Router search parameters.
findings.preconditions: Attacker induces native/web client to open/navigate affected Router path with sufficiently malformed percent-encoded query string; no backend request is required.
findings.impact: Client/web runtime availability degradation or unresponsiveness. Advisory does not describe confidentiality, integrity, or code execution impact.
findings.remediation: Qualify Expo Router/Expo SDK parent migration with compatible fixed graph; do not directly override decoder, add wrapper, or use CommonJS bridge.
findings.acceptance: Frozen-lock install, fresh production audit, and bounded hostile deep-link regression demonstrate removal and compatible consumer behavior.
findings.reachability: Native/web deep-link parsing.
findings.approval_boundary: No exploit payload, app start, or device test was executed.

findings.domain: Locked dependency advisories and compatibility exposure
findings.title: Expo CLI retains vulnerable Zod 3 for tooling schemas
evidence: raw/pnpm-audit-production.json:267-338 reports transitive zod@3.25.76; direct application zod is 4.6.7 at package.json:103 and pnpm-lock.yaml:209-211,6268-6269.
pnpm-lock.yaml:7307 resolves affected copy under @expo/cli@57.0.26; node_modules/@expo/cli/build/src/start/server/DevToolsPlugin.schema.js:19-47,82 contains unbounded arrays.
package.json:12,33 exposes Expo tooling and .github/workflows/ci.yml:231-235 invokes expo export; server/_core/index.ts:1-25 imports no Expo CLI.
findings.preconditions: Expo tooling/build execution reaches affected unbounded CLI schema with attacker-controlled oversized array input.
findings.impact: Potential resource exhaustion in local development or CI tooling; production server/API invocation was not established.
findings.remediation: Wait for/qualify Expo CLI parent release or SDK migration; do not force Zod 4 into CLI's 3.x dependency range.
findings.acceptance: Fresh production audit and installed CLI-consumer coverage prove a qualified parent removes the affected resolution.
findings.reachability: Development and CI tooling, not established production server/API.
findings.approval_boundary: No CLI schema exploit/build was run.

findings.domain: Locked dependency advisories and compatibility exposure
findings.title: Expo code-signing tooling contains the unpatched node-forge signature verifier
evidence: raw/pnpm-audit-production.json:158-265 reports node-forge@1.4.0; pnpm-lock.yaml:7289,7324-7326,4878-4880 places it under Expo CLI/code-signing certificates.
node_modules/@expo/code-signing-certificates/build/main.js:153-207 verifies self-signed certificates/signatures and :235-247 verifies CSR input.
server/_core/index.ts:1-25 does not import tooling; no deployment signing path or untrusted certificate input was exercised.
findings.preconditions: Development, CI, or code-signing operation invokes affected verification with crafted certificate, signature, or CSR.
findings.impact: Forged-signature acceptance could undermine code-signing integrity decision if the condition is met; present deployment use is unproven.
findings.remediation: Qualify Expo/CLI or code-signing-consumer parent update removing/replacing resolver, or SDK migration; do not write custom RSA/ASN.1 handling.
findings.acceptance: Qualified parent removal is evidenced by fresh audit and consumer regression; advisory-specific crafted input is evaluated only in approved test scope.
findings.reachability: Development/CI/signing tooling; not established production API reachability.
findings.approval_boundary: No signing workflow was run.

findings.domain: Locked dependency advisories and compatibility exposure
findings.title: Expo configuration merging retains unpatched deepmerge prototype-poisoning exposure
evidence: raw/pnpm-audit-production.json:340-587 reports deepmerge@4.3.1; pnpm-lock.yaml:3109-3111,7353-7356 resolves @expo/config@57.0.9 > deepmerge@4.3.1.
node_modules/@expo/config/build/Config.js:40-45,407-453 imports/merges root config modifications and plugin properties.
app.config.ts:29-40,63-177 contains dynamic application config/plugin objects; CI runs Expo export, but no app request-to-config merge path was found.
findings.preconditions: Attacker introduces a malicious source object into Expo configuration modifications/plugin properties during build/config evaluation.
findings.impact: Conditional build/tooling integrity exposure via prototype poisoning; no remote production API sink or app-runtime exploit path was established.
findings.remediation: Keep configuration/CI inputs trusted and reviewed; qualify @expo/config/Expo parent update only when it removes affected resolution and add installed-consumer merge regression.
findings.acceptance: Fresh production audit and benign installed consumer regression demonstrate qualified parent graph change.
findings.reachability: Configuration/build tooling, not established request-driven production path.
findings.approval_boundary: No Expo export/build was started.

findings.preconditions: Release/remediation decision relies on dated documentation instead of fresh raw audit evidence.

findings.remediation: At next authorized documentation refresh, record fresh raw audit timestamp/hashes, add deepmerge GHSA, and label historic cache advisory non-emitted rather than remediated.
findings.acceptance: Dependency register aligns family/version/status with fresh audit, separates direct/runtime/tooling reachability, and records audit artifact identity.
findings.reachability: Security governance and release decision-making.
findings.approval_boundary: No dependency document was edited as part of domain review; this reconciled register records the gap.

limitations: No production credentials, provider or live database requests, live catalog reads/writes, migrations, production application/service starts, key rotation, publication, or production operations occurred. Tests can start disposable local subprocesses/listeners and synthetic recovery fixtures; this task writes audit documentation only.

No real ingress/CDN/WAF, TLS termination, CORS browser matrix, object provider, deployed DNS/CDN/TLS, native device, camera/microphone, real WebRTC/TURN, backup archive, restore, signing, or provider configuration was exercised.

Source/static/mocked tests cannot establish deployed PostgreSQL locks/RLS/query plans, external rate limiting, browser/WebView cookie behavior, native cache/decoder behavior, or modified-client media behavior.
